overview: The Medford Traffic Commission regulates parking regulations, permit programs, traffic flow, and roadway safety across the city of Medford. The commission's record in the archive covers 13 meetings held between December 2023 and September 2026. Throughout this period, the body has decided on residential permit variances, established transit parking zones, updated fee schedules, and enacted safety measures such as crosswalk daylighting. It also collaborates with municipal departments to manage commercial vehicle parking, emergency access clearances, and electric vehicle charging locations. At its most recent meeting, the commission enacted emergency vehicle tow zones, increased visitor pass replacement fees, and approved multiple intersection safety restrictions (M13#10, M13#12, M13#14).

threads.name: Transit area residential parking zones
threads.summary: In April 2024, the commission approved a one-year pilot program for a unified resident parking zone in South Medford to manage parking demand near Green Line transit stations (M04#2). The commission scheduled a formal review of the program for early 2025 (M08#14). Following a trial period with zero formal complaints and active enforcement, the commission voted to make the G-Zone residential parking program permanent (M09#15).

threads.name: Residential parking permit variances
threads.summary: The commission routinely evaluates variance requests from residents lacking off-street parking or living on unpermitted main streets who seek permits for adjacent side streets (M01#8, M02#3, M04#4). In October 2024, the body streamlined its workflow by adopting a policy that makes residential parking variances permanent for current residents as long as permits are maintained (M05#10). Despite this administrative policy, the commission continues to consider individual petitions and grant location-specific variances (M11#7, M12#3, M13#2).

threads.name: Commercial vehicle parking restrictions
threads.summary: To prevent commercial trucks and local businesses from using public streets for long-term vehicle storage, the commission instituted overnight parking bans on major corridors like Commercial Street and Mystic Avenue (M01#7, M02#9). The body occasionally granted temporary variances for commercial work vehicles (M01#4), but later denied multiple commercial variance requests by citing a city ordinance prohibiting overnight commercial street parking (M09#8). In July 2025, the commission initiated discussions on updating regulations to allow residential permits for certain smaller commercial vehicles, referring the proposal for public outreach (M10#5).

threads.name: Crosswalk daylighting and intersection sightlines
threads.summary: The commission frequently approves parking restrictions near intersections and crosswalks to improve driver visibility and pedestrian safety. Early interventions established no-parking safety buffer zones at intersections like Fulton Street and Spring Street (M04#6). The commission expanded these measures to daylight crosswalks near Kellis Field and Lawrence Road (M05#3, M06#7), and near High Street following traffic safety concerns (M09#13, M12#10). Later meetings saw additional corner parking offsets approved across the Hancock Street area to maintain clear sightlines (M13#14).

threads.name: Emergency vehicle clearance and access
threads.summary: The commission acts on requests from the Fire Department and public safety officials to clear narrow streets and tight turns for emergency apparatus. In late 2023, the body created a tow zone on Foss Street to ensure emergency vehicles could pass safely (M01#3). It later implemented a chicane parking layout on Pearl Street to formalize legal parking while ensuring emergency vehicle access (M10#4). In September 2026, the commission designated tow zones on Metcalf Street and Elliott Street after receiving evidence of fire engines getting stuck on sharp turns (M13#10, M13#11).

threads.name: On-street electric vehicle charging infrastructure
threads.summary: In September 2025, the commission reviewed a grant-funded proposal to install on-street electric vehicle charging stations near five city parks, taking public comment on potential impacts to neighborhood parking (M11#10). The following month, the commission approved installing two on-street charging stations near 200 Boston Avenue as a compromise location for residents without off-street parking (M12#2).

periods.narrative: During this period, the commission granted accessible parking spaces, established parking rules on Foss and Park Streets, and limited overnight commercial vehicle parking.

The commission approved and permanently established the G-Zone transit parking program, updated parking permit fee schedules, and implemented extensive crosswalk daylighting and intersection safety measures across the city.
The commission addressed emergency apparatus navigation requirements, increased replacement fees for lost visitor passes, and established local resident parking regulations and stop signs.
